'''Matthew Houghton Todd''' (born 13 January 1973) is a British [[chemist]] and the Professor and Chair of [[Drug Discovery]] of the [[UCL School of Pharmacy|School of Pharmacy]] at [[University College London]].<ref name="UCL">{{cite web |title=Professor Matthew Todd – UCL School of Pharmacy |date=2 October 2018 |url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/pharmacy/people/professor-matthew-todd}}</ref> He is the founder of Open Source Malaria (OSM) and his research focuses on [[drug discovery]] and development for this disease.<ref name="OSM2">{{cite news |last1=Peplow |first1=M |title=Open-source drug discovery takes aim at malaria and neglected diseases |url=https://cen.acs.org/pharmaceuticals/drug-discovery/Open-source-drug-discovery-takes-aim-at-malaria-and-neglected-diseases/97/i5 |access-date=13 February 2019 |work=C&EN |publisher=ACS |year=2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Lowe |first1=D |title=The Open Source Malaria Project, So Far |url=https://www.science.org/content/blog-post/open-source-malaria-project-so-far |access-date=13 February 2019 |work=In The Pipeline }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Williamson |first1=AE |title=Open Source Drug Discovery: Highly Potent Antimalarial Compounds Derived from the Tres Cantos Arylpyrroles |journal=ACS Central Science |year=2016 |volume=2 |issue=10 |pages=687–701 |doi=10.1021/acscentsci.6b00086  |doi-access=free|pmid=27800551 |pmc=5084075 }}</ref><ref name="OSM1">{{cite journal |last1=Robertson |first1=MN |title=Open source drug discovery – A limited tutorial |journal=Parasitology |year=2014 |volume=141 |issue=1 |pages=148–157 |doi=10.1017/S0031182013001121 |pmid=23985301 |pmc=3884843 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tse |first1=EG |last2=Korsik |first2=M |last3=Todd |first3=MH |title=The past, present and future of anti-malarial medicines |journal=Malaria Journal |year=2019 |volume=18 |issue=1 |page=93 |doi=10.1186/s12936-019-2724-z |pmid=30902052 |pmc=6431062 |doi-access=free }}</ref> Recently, he has expanded to other areas, particularly neglected diseases such as [[tuberculosis]] and [[mycetoma]]<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lim |first1=W |title=Addressing the most neglected diseases through an open research model: The discovery of fenarimols as novel drug candidates for eumycetoma |journal=PLOS Neglected Tropical Diseases |year=2018 |volume=12 |issue=2 |article-number=e0006437 |doi=10.1371/journal.pntd.0006437 |pmid=29698504 |pmc=5940239 |doi-access=free }}</ref> in the Open Source Tuberculosis (OSTB) and Open Source Mycetoma (MycetOS) project, through a collaboration with the [[Drugs for Neglected Diseases Initiative]] and [[Erasmus MC]].<ref>{{cite web |title=MycetOS – DNDi |date=31 December 2017 |url=https://www.dndi.org/diseases-projects/open-innovation/mycetos/}}</ref> In addition, he has some research activity in [[catalysis]] and [[methodology]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Park |first1=SJ |title=Oxidative Arylation of Isochroman |journal=Journal of Organic Chemistry |year=2002 |volume=77 |issue=2 |pages=949–955 |doi=10.1021/jo2021373 |pmid=22142205 |url=https://figshare.com/articles/Oxidative_Arylation_of_Isochroman/2557438 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tsang |first1=ASK |title=Facile synthesis of vicinal diamines via oxidation of N-phenyltetrahydroisoquinolines with DDQ |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |year=2009 |volume=50 |issue=11 |pages=1199–1202 |doi=10.1016/j.tetlet.2008.12.101 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hashmi |first1=ASK |title=Gold-Catalysis: Reactions of Organogold Compounds with Electrophiles |journal=Australian Journal of Chemistry |year=2010 |volume=63 |issue=12 |pages=1619–1626 |doi=10.1071/CH10342 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Ahamed |first1=M |title=Catalytic Asymmetric Additions of Carbon-Centered Nucleophiles to Nitrogen-Containing Aromatic Heterocycles |journal=European Journal of Organic Chemistry |year=2010 |volume=2010 |issue=31 |pages=5935–5942 |doi=10.1002/ejoc.201000877 }}</ref>

== Education ==

Todd received an [[Master of Arts (Oxford, Cambridge, and Dublin)|MA]] in [[Natural Sciences Tripos|Natural Sciences]] from the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1995. He obtained his PhD in [[Organic Chemistry]] at the same institution in 1999, working with [[Chris Abell]] on encoding and linker strategies for [[combinatorial chemistry]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Todd |first1=MH |title=Studies on the synthesis, characterisation and reactivity of aromatic diboronic acids |journal=Tetrahedron Letters |year=1997 |volume=38 |issue=38 |pages=6781–6784 |doi=10.1016/S0040-4039(97)01552-9 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Todd |first1=MH |title=Novel chemical tagging method for combinatorial synthesis utilizing Suzuki chemistry and Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry |journal=Journal of Combinatorial Chemistry |year=2001 |volume=3 |issue=3 |pages=319–327 |doi=10.1021/cc000112m |pmid=11350256 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Todd |first1=MH |title=A novel safety-catch linker for the solid-phase synthesis of amides and esters |journal=Organic Letters |year=1999 |volume=1 |issue=8 |pages=1149–1151 |doi=10.1021/ol990785h }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Past Members - The Abell Group |url=https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/group/abell/past-members |access-date=12 February 2019 |archive-date=22 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200922174813/https://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/group/abell/past-members |url-status=dead }}</ref> Todd was a [[Wellcome Trust]] [[Postdoctoral researcher|Postdoctoral Research Fellow]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] from 1999 to 2000, working with Paul A. Bartlett on synthesis of amino acid-derived [[Heterocyclic compound|heterocycles]] by [[Lewis acid catalysis]] and [[radical cyclisation]]s from peptide acetals.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Todd |first1=MH |title=Amino acid derived heterocycles: Lewis acid catalyzed and radical cyclizations from peptide acetals |journal=Journal of Organic Chemistry |year=2002 |volume=67 |issue=12 |pages=3985–3988 |doi=10.1021/jo010990m |pmid=12054930 |url=https://figshare.com/articles/journal_contribution/3690723 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Paul A. Bartlett Group Alumni |url=http://www.cchem.berkeley.edu/pabgrp/People/Former.html |access-date=12 February 2019}}</ref>

== Career and research ==

From 2000 to 2001, he was a [[Fellow|College Fellow]] and Lecturer at New Hall, Cambridge (now [[Murray Edwards College, Cambridge]]). He began his independent research career in 2001 at [[Queen Mary University of London]]. In 2005, he relocated to Australia where he was a lecturer, [[senior lecturer]], then [[associate professor]] at the [[University of Sydney School of Chemistry|School of Chemistry]], [[University of Sydney]]. In 2018, he returned to the United Kingdom to take the role of professor and Chair of Drug Discovery at [[University College London|UCL]] [[UCL School of Pharmacy|School of Pharmacy]].<ref name="UCL"/>

In response to the price hike of [[HIV/AIDS]] drug, [[pyrimethamine]] (Daraprim), by [[Turing Pharmaceuticals]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Timmerman |first1=L |title=A Timeline of the Turing Pharma Controversy |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/luketimmerman/2015/09/23/a-timeline-of-the-turing-pharma-controversy/ |access-date=12 February 2019 |work=Forbes}}</ref> Todd and the Open Source Malaria team led a small team of high school students from [[Sydney Grammar School]] to synthesise the drug.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Reiner |first1=V |title=Students make $750 drug cheaply with Open Source Malaria team |url=https://sydney.edu.au/news-opinion/news/2016/11/30/students-make--750-drug-cheaply-with-open-source-malaria-team-.html |access-date=13 February 2019 |publisher=University of Sydney |date=30 November 2016}}</ref><ref name="Daraprim2">{{cite news |last1=Davey |first1=M |title=Australian students recreate Martin Shkreli price-hike drug in school lab |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2016/dec/01/australian-students-recreate-martin-shkreli-price-hike-drug-in-school-lab |access-date=12 February 2019 |work=The Guardian}}</ref> The students produced 3.7 grams of [[pyrimethamine]] for US$20, which would be worth between US$35,000 and US$110,000 in the United States based on hiked prices.<ref name="Daraprim">{{cite news |last1=Hunjan |first1=R |title=Daraprim drug's key ingredient recreated by high school students in Sydney for just $20 |url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2016-11-30/daraprim-nsw-students-create-drug-martin-shkreli-sold/8078892 |access-date=12 February 2019 |publisher=ABC}}</ref> This received significant media attention and was featured on [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC]],<ref name="Daraprim" /> [[BBC]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dunlop |first1=G |title=Martin Shkreli: Australian boys recreate life-saving drug |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-australia-38153254 |access-date=12 February 2019 |publisher=BBC}}</ref> [[CNN]],<ref>{{cite news |last1=Roberts |first1=E |title='Pharma Bro' Martin Shkreli meets his match in a group of Australian schoolboys |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2016/12/01/health/daraprim-oz/index.html |access-date=12 February 2019 |publisher=CNN}}</ref> [[The Guardian]],<ref name="Daraprim2" /> and [[Time (magazine)|Time]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Watch Martin Shkreli Respond to the School Kids Who Recreated His Drug for $2 a Dose |last1=Lui |first1=K |url=https://time.com/4588458/martin-shkreli-response-sydney-students-daraprim/ |magazine=Time |access-date=17 November 2024 |archive-date=3 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201103185003/https://time.com/4588458/martin-shkreli-response-sydney-students-daraprim/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Todd has been a vocal proponent of [[open science]] and [[open research]].<ref name="OSM2" /><ref name="OSM1" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Woelfle |first1=M |title=Open science is a research accelerator |journal=Nature Chemistry |year=2011 |volume=3 |issue=10 |pages=745–748 |doi=10.1038/nchem.1149 |pmid=21941234 |bibcode=2011NatCh...3..745W |s2cid=205289283 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Laursen |first1=L |title=Tropical disease: A neglected cause |journal=Nature |year=2016 |volume=533 |issue=7602 |pages=S68–S69 |doi=10.1038/533S68a |pmid=27167396 |bibcode=2016Natur.533S..68L |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Anderson |first1=T |title=Can open-source drug development deliver? |journal=The Lancet |year=2016 |volume=387 |issue=10032 |pages=1983–1984 |doi=10.1016/S0140-6736(16)30518-9 |pmid=27203757 |s2cid=44792421 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Todd |first1=MH |title=Why open source pharma is the path to both new and cheaper medicines |url=https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2017/apr/19/why-open-source-pharma-is-the-path-to-both-cheaper-and-new-medicines |work=The Guardian |access-date=12 February 2019}}</ref> In 2011, he proposed Six Laws of Open Research to guide present and future open research projects including OSM and MycetOS:<ref name="OSM1" /><ref>{{cite web |last1=Todd |first1=MH |title=Open Source Drug Discovery for Malaria |url=http://www.thesynapticleap.org/node/343 |access-date=12 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Pearce |first1=R |title=Researchers look to open source to tackle deadly infection |url=https://www.computerworld.com.au/article/632476/researchers-look-open-source-help-tackle-deadly-infection/ |access-date=12 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Open Source Research – OpenWetWare |url=https://openwetware.org/wiki/Open_Source_Research |access-date=12 February 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Williamson |first1=AE |title=Open science: the future of research? |url=http://www.abc.net.au/science/articles/2015/06/29/4254093.htm |access-date=12 February 2019 |publisher=ABC}}</ref>

{{blockquote|

# All data are open and all ideas are shared.
# Anyone can take part at any level of the project.
# There will be no patents.
# Suggestions are the best form of criticism.
# Public discussion is much more valuable than private email.
# The project is bigger than, and is not owned by, any given lab. The aim is to find a good drug for malaria, by whatever means, as quickly as possible.}}

Todd is on the [[Editorial board]]s of Chemistry Central Journal,<ref>{{cite web |title=Chemistry Central Journal (Editorial Board) |url=https://www.springer.com/chemistry/journal/13065?detailsPage=editorialBoard |access-date=12 February 2019 |website=Chemistry Central Journal |archive-date=21 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621170757/https://www.springer.com/chemistry/journal/13065?detailsPage=editorialBoard |url-status=dead }}</ref> ChemistryOpen,<ref>{{cite web |title=Editorial Advisory Board |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/page/journal/21911363/homepage/2011_edbd.html |website=ChemistryOpen |access-date=12 February 2019}}</ref> [[PLOS One]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Editorial Board |url=https://journals.plos.org/plosone/static/editorial-board |website=PLOS ONE |access-date=12 February 2019}}</ref> [[Scientific Reports]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Editorial Advisory Panel and Editorial Board |url=https://www.nature.com/srep/about/editorial-board#chemistry |website=Scientific Reports |access-date=12 February 2019}}</ref> and [[Scientific Data (journal)|Scientific Data]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Editors, Advisory Panel & Editorial Board |url=https://www.nature.com/sdata/about/editorial-board |website=Scientific Data |access-date=12 February 2019}}</ref>
